player.prompt:
Create a NEW hand-painted production game animation sheet of Alick. The first reference is authoritative ONLY for frame order, camera, screen direction, placement and body articulation. The second reference is the NEW authoritative full-resolution costume and face model: carefully repaint EVERY frame in its colours, anatomy, materials and observed naturalist illustration style. The slim young adult deckhand from the references has a short dark beard, a charcoal-blue ribbed watch cap, a strong ochre neckcloth tucked into a work-softened slate-indigo pea jacket, warm smoke-brown wool trousers and worn tar-brown ankle boots. Give his narrow jaw, skin and thoughtful eyes individual character. His jacket is blue, never green. Deliver ONE very wide transparent sprite sheet with EXACTLY THREE separate painted figures occupying left, middle and right in one horizontal row. Strictly match the three gestures, anchors and proportions of reference 1 without adding a prop: LEFT is a fully upright, calm side-on stance with both boots flat. CENTRE is a balanced shallow bend with both forearms reaching right towards a waist-high work surface. RIGHT is the lower one-knee crouch with the forward hand extended right and down towards a ground object. Match reference 1 closely: same boot support, same extension of the palm and fingertip, same crown, same angle of head, same location of leading knee, both arms and all feet visible. Reproduce negative space between legs and arms. All faces look screen RIGHT. Keep ONE height scale, same hat or hair and same head size in all three, so the crouch occupies about 62% as much vertical height as the stand. Keep all soles on their common baseline. Full empty transparent gutters between the poses. No extra poses or simultaneous character copies within a pose.
 
Paint the character with the second reference's crisp graphite underdrawing and rich naturalist 1860s maritime gouache: brushwork held together in broad, legible local colour shapes at reduced size, worn wool, hand-sewn linen, scuffed boots, warm skin under a cool upper-left sky. Preserve pronounced local jacket colour and skin tone across every cell. Keep the same stitches, buttons, creases and cap through all cells; make every mark feel part of the same painted world. Avoid dull uniformly brown or uniformly green wash. No independent character redesign, no changes of coat, expressions or cap. Empty hands, no bags, no separate items, NO text, grid lines, floor, shadow, backdrop or digital airbrush glow; absolutely transparent pixels outside and between the character silhouettes. Historical art direction is an original reconstruction for an adventure game.
